# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L175


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Pausable unstake/withdraws can be dangerous as they restrict users in the case of an emergency, like a hack - when withdraws are most needed.

## Proof of Concept
[unstakeMunchable](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L175) is pausable:

```solidity
    function unstakeMunchable(uint256 tokenId) external override forceFarmPlots(msg.sender) notPaused {
```

However having pausability on critical user functions like unstake is dangerous as it can lead to pretty bad scenarios in the cases of a hack. Needing to unpause the whole system in order for users to withdraw will enable the hacker to exploit it even more.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Removed the `notPaused` modifier.

```diff
-    function unstakeMunchable(uint256 tokenId) external override forceFarmPlots(msg.sender) notPaused {
+    function unstakeMunchable(uint256 tokenId) external override forceFarmPlots(msg.sender) {
```

Another solution is to make 2 pause mods, normal - pausing everything but unstake, and emergency - pausing the whole system.


## Assessed type

Error

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L270


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Players and landlords with unclaimed rewards will receive a different amount based on the change.

## Proof of Concept
`BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE`, `REALM_BONUSES` and `RARITY_BONUSES` are all global parameters set by the config. However since they are not immutable it is presumed that if there is a need they can be changed to whatever the system sees fit.

```solidity
    uint256 BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE;
    uint256 PRICE_PER_PLOT;
    int16[] REALM_BONUSES;
    uint8[] RARITY_BONUSES;
```

However altering these variables will have an effect on all generated, but not yet claimed rewards. That is because [_farmPlots](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L270-L286) in a way generates reward time, which is multiplied by `BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE` to get the reward amount. Changing this value will have an effect, be it positive or negative, on all unclaimed rewards.

Same can be said for the rest of previously mentioned variables.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Take into account such behavior when changing these variables. 


## Assessed type

Error

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L345


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The `_getNumPlots` function in the Munchables `LandManager` contract is used to get the plots of land a landlord owns using the formula `_getNumPlots = lockManager.getLockedWeightedValue(_account) / PRICE_PER_PLOT;` due to rounding down in solidity this disfavors landlords and disincentivizes land ownership.


## Proof of Concept
the `getLockedWeightedValue` in the above formula "Calculates the USD value of all tokens locked by a player, weighted by their yield" and is used at several locations in the codebase

Consider the following case, Landlord locks Tokens worth 30USD(plus yield) in the `LockManager`, and the price per_plot is 30USD , in this case, according to `_getNumPlots` landlord has 1 plot of land, any even the most minuscle fluctuation in value of locked tokens to 29.99USD now means the landlord has 0 land allocated, even when the same number of token is still locked.
In solidity 
_getNumPlots = 29/30 = 0 plots of land

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Protocol should round in favor of `landlords` to incentivize land ownership, small fluctuations in price should not change the status quo.


## Assessed type

Math

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L145-L146


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The incorrect plot range check can cause transactions to fail due to a wrongly implemented validation, while we have both the plot and the NFT. This disrupts the staking process, leading to losing the opportunity for both parties, staker and landlord.

## Proof of Concept

The issue lies in the incorrect validation of the plot range, which can cause transactions to fail even when both the plot and the NFT are available.

```solidity
uint256 totalPlotsAvail = _getNumPlots(landlord);
if (plotId >= totalPlotsAvail) revert PlotTooHighError();
```
```solidity
function _getNumPlots(address _account) internal view returns (uint256) {
   return lockManager.getLockedWeightedValue(_account) / PRICE_PER_PLOT;
}
```
The current validation uses >=, which incorrectly allows for the possibility of staking to an invalid plot index.
This results in a transaction failure despite having both the plot and the NFT available.

**Example scenario:**

Let's consider a scenario where the landlord has exactly one plot. This means totalPlotsAvail will be 1.

Landlord: Has only one plot.
Staker: Attempts to stake an NFT to plotId 1.

This scenario will lead to a failed transaction, causing the staking process to be disrupted. Both the staker and the landlord lose the opportunity to:

1. Earn Points: The staking process is tied to farming points or other incentives. By failing to stake, both parties miss out on potential rewards and benefits.
2. Utilize Assets: Despite having the necessary plot and NFT, the faulty validation prevents their proper use, leading to frustration and inefficiency.

## Tools Used

Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

By correcting the condition to use >, we ensure the plot index is correctly validated:
```solidity
if (plotId > totalPlotsAvail) revert PlotTooHighError();
```



## Assessed type

Invalid Validation

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L272
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L278


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The `LandManager::_farmPlots(...)` can potentially revert due to `Index out of bounds` error, if the global `REALM_BONUSES` or `RARITY_BONUSES` arrays are not properly set.

## Proof of Concept
The `LandManager.sol` contract allows users to stake their munchables to other users' plots, in order to farm schnibbles. The schnibble rewards are increased with a bonus, which is formed from various user and NFT attributes. The calculation of this bonus is based on the `REALM_BONUSES` and `RARITY_BONUSES` arrays, which are set prior to deployment:

```solidity
function _farmPlots(address _sender) internal {
       __SNIP
    finalBonus =
        int16(
@>            REALM_BONUSES[
                (uint256(immutableAttributes.realm) * 5) +
                    uint256(landlordMetadata.snuggeryRealm)
            ]
        ) +
        int16(
@>            int8(RARITY_BONUSES[uint256(immutableAttributes.rarity)])
        );
    __SNIP__
}
```

If the values in these arrays are misconfiguted, then the current calculation for the indexes will fail for specific realm and rarity combinations, leading to `_farmPlots()` to always revert, blocking all functionalities in the `LandManager` contract. This has been properly handled in the [BonusManager::getFeedBonus(...)](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/BonusManager.sol#L102-L112) function, meaning that the dev elopment team are aware of such a problem.

## Tools Used

Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Use the same index checks as done in the [BonusManager::getFeedBonus(...)](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/BonusManager.sol#L102-L112) function, but instead of reverting set a default value.

```diff
+++ b/src/managers/LandManager.sol
@@ -267,15 +267,17 @@ contract LandManager is BaseBlastManagerUpgradeable, ILandManager {
             immutableAttributes = nftAttributesManager.getImmutableAttributes(
                 tokenId
             );
+            uint256 realmIndex = (uint256(immutableAttributes.realm) * 5) +
+                uint256(landlordMetadata.snuggeryRealm);
+            if (realmIndex >= REALM_BONUSES.length)
+                realmIndex = DEFAULT_REALM_BONUS_INDEX;
+            uint256 rarityIndex = uint256(immutableAttributes.rarity);
+            if (rarityIndex >= RARITY_BONUSES.length)
+                rarityIndex = DEFAULT_RARITY_BONUS_INDEX;
             finalBonus =
+                int16(REALM_BONUSES[realmIndex]) +
                 int16(
-                    REALM_BONUSES[
-                        (uint256(immutableAttributes.realm) * 5) +
-                            uint256(landlordMetadata.snuggeryRealm)
-                    ]
-                ) +
-                int16(
-                    int8(RARITY_BONUSES[uint256(immutableAttributes.rarity)])
+                    int8(RARITY_BONUSES[rarityIndex])
                 );
             schnibblesTotal =
                 (timestamp - _toiler.lastToilDate) *
```


## Assessed type

DoS

warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L88-L90
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L65-L69
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L166
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L292-L293


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
If LandLord have larger `taxRate` than `MAX_TAX_RATE` this will make him get more `taxes` than the currently Set Max which will benefit him beneficialy leading to more schnibbles taken for him from users staked at him

If LandLord have smaller `taxRate` than `MIN_TAX_RATE`, this will give him more advantages to attract other users to stake on him and not on other new LandLords that are forced by the new `MIN_TAX_RATE`


## Proof of Concept

The problem lies in the fact that the way the `TaxRate` is reconfugered doesn't backward affect the LandLords who already have set their `TaxRate` 

This makes it like the LandLord now has the choice to update his `currentTaxRate` to `MAX` or `MIN` if it only benefates him directly or indirectly. This even can be grouped with the fact that LandLord can frontRun the `_reconfigure` to his intent

**For example:**
- LandLord is having his taxRate at 75e16 `MAX`
- trusted entity updates the `MAX_TAX_RATE` to 60e16
- `plotMetadata[landlord].currentTaxRate` is yet still have 75e16 as its value.

Same thing for `MinTaxRate` that can be gamed as mentioned in Impact section

In fact the LandLord can have another scenario:
- LandLord is having his taxRate at 50e16(not MAX) while `Max` is at 75e16
- trusted party sumbit a txn to updates the `MAX_TAX_RATE` to 60e16
- LandLord sees this as an opportunity that won't be made again and frontruns that trusted entity txn and set his `taxRate` at 75e16 `MAX`
- The txn of the trusted entity gets executed and update the `MAX` to 60e16
- `plotMetadata[landlord].currentTaxRate` is yet still have 75e16 as its value.



## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
to prevent the LandLord from beneficially having his rate to be outdated we can make condition `if` (which is `?`) whenever we use the `plotMetadata[landlord].currentTaxRate` in any function

when ever we set the `currentTaxRate` to any staker during `stakeMunchable` or `_farmPlots` we check if `currentTaxRate` < `MIN_TAX_RATE`? if true then we set `latestTaxRate` of that staked `tokenId` to `MIN_TAX_RATE` and also the same check for if > `MAX_TAX_RATE`


## Assessed type

Context

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L232


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Users can occupy the plot for a long time but do not allow the landowner to receive Schnibbles.

## Proof of Concept
background:
1. The user will occupy the landowner's plot, and then receive Schnibbles through the `_farmPlots` function. The Schnibbles will be distributed to the user and the landowner in proportion.
2. In the `_farmPlots` function, [whether a piece of land is dirty is determined based on the landlord's pledge. If it is dirty, Schnibbles will not be updated after this time](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L258-L261).

There are two situations where users can prevent landowners from receiving Schnibbles.
1. The user never receives Schnibbles but always occupies this plot.
2. After the landlord withdraws the funds, the polt becomes dirty, and the landlord stakes again. The land will not become non-dirty. Schnibbles no longer spawn. Users can occupy the plot without taking out the NFT.

User failure to claim may be malicious or unintentional.
Since there is a risk of funds being locked, it satisfies High, but the possibility is low because users do not get rewards. So I think the risk is Med.

## Tools Used
manual

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
It is recommended that landowners also call the `farmPlots` function to receive Schnibbles.


## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The LandManager contract retains approval to transfer NFTs even after they have been unstaked. This persistent approval presents several risks:

1. Unexpected Control: Users may assume that unstaking an NFT removes all permissions, but the LandManager can still transfer their NFT.
2. Increased Attack Surface: If the LandManager contract is compromised in the future, it could affect NFTs that users believe are fully under their control.
3. Reduced NFT Liquidity: Potential buyers on secondary markets may be hesitant to purchase NFTs with existing approvals, potentially impacting the asset's value.
4. User Trust: This behavior contradicts user expectations, potentially eroding trust in the platform.

While users can manually revoke approvals, this requires extra steps and knowledge that many users may not have, making it a suboptimal solution from a user experience perspective.

## Proof of Concept
The issue occurs in the `unstakeMunchable` function of the LandManager contract:


```solidity
function unstakeMunchable(uint256 tokenId) external override forceFarmPlots(msg.sender) notPaused {
    // ... existing code ...
    munchNFT.transferFrom(address(this), mainAccount, tokenId);
    // Approval is not revoked here
    emit FarmPlotLeave(_toiler.landlord, tokenId, _toiler.plotId);
}
```

To demonstrate:

1. User stakes their NFT, approving the LandManager.
2. User unstakes their NFT using `unstakeMunchable`.
3. The NFT is returned to the user, but the LandManager's approval remains.
4. The LandManager can still transfer the NFT without further approval.


## Tools Used
VS code
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Add an approval revocation step in the `unstakeMunchable` function:

```solidity
function unstakeMunchable(uint256 tokenId) external override forceFarmPlots(msg.sender) notPaused {
    // ... existing code ...
    munchNFT.transferFrom(address(this), mainAccount, tokenId);
    munchNFT.approve(address(0), tokenId);  // Revoke approval
    emit FarmPlotLeave(_toiler.landlord, tokenId, _toiler.plotId);
}
```

This ensures that the LandManager's approval is removed when the NFT is unstaked, aligning with user expectations and reducing potential security risks.

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L344


# Vulnerability details

## Description
The `getNumPlots` function uses integer division to calculate plot allocation, which can lead to the loss of significant value due to truncation, especially given the high `PRICE_PER_PLOT`.

## Code snippet
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L344
```solidity
function getNumPlots(address _account) internal view returns (uint256) {
    return lockManager.getLockedWeightedValue(_account) / PRICE_PER_PLOT;
}
```

The `PRICE_PER_PLOT` is set to 30 ETH (30e18 wei).

## Problem
Integer division in Solidity truncates any remainder. With `PRICE_PER_PLOT` at 30 ETH, users could potentially lose up to 29.99... ETH worth of value without receiving a corresponding plot. This becomes significant when dealing with large locked values.

For example:
- If a user locks 89 ETH, they will receive 2 plots (89 / 30 = 2.96..., truncated to 2).
- The user effectively loses the benefit of 29 ETH of their locked value.

## Impact
While this issue affects all users, it's particularly impactful for:
1. Users locking large amounts of value.
2. The protocol itself, which may accumulate substantial "unused" locked value over time.

The high `PRICE_PER_PLOT` means that each instance of truncation can represent a significant amount of value (up to 29.99... ETH).

## Suggested Fixes

1. Implement a credit system:

```solidity
mapping(address => uint256) public plotCredits;

function getNumPlots(address _account) internal returns (uint256) {
    uint256 totalValue = lockManager.getLockedWeightedValue(_account) + plotCredits[_account];
    uint256 plots = totalValue / PRICE_PER_PLOT;
    plotCredits[_account] = totalValue % PRICE_PER_PLOT;
    return plots;
}
```
This system accumulates "change" for future plot purchases.

2. Allow fractional plot ownership:

Consider implementing a system where users can own fractions of plots, represented as a separate token or within the existing NFT structure.


3. Rounding up (with caution):

```solidity
function getNumPlots(address _account) internal view returns (uint256) {
    uint256 lockedValue = lockManager.getLockedWeightedValue(_account);
    return (lockedValue + PRICE_PER_PLOT - 1) / PRICE_PER_PLOT;
}
```

Note: This approach always favors the user and may need additional mechanisms to prevent exploitation.

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/94cf468aaabf526b7a8319f7eba34014ccebe7b9/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L287


# Vulnerability details

## Description
The calculation of the landlord's share of schnibbles may result in significant precision loss due to integer division, particularly when dealing with small values of `schnibblesTotal`.


## Code snippet

```solidity
schnibblesLandlord = (schnibblesTotal * _toiler.latestTaxRate) / 1e18;
```

The use of integer division in Solidity truncates any remainder. When `schnibblesTotal` is small relative to the tax rate (which is scaled by 1e18), the result of this calculation could be zero, even when a non-zero amount should be allocated to the landlord.

For instance, if `schnibblesTotal` is 1000 and `_toiler.latestTaxRate` is 1e16 (1%), the calculation would result in:
(1000 * 1e16) / 1e18 = 0

This means the landlord receives nothing, even though they should receive 1% of 1000, which is 10.

## Impact
1. Landlords may not receive their fair share of schnibbles, especially for small amounts or short time periods.
2. This could disincentivize landlords from participating in the system, particularly those with lower tax rates.
3. Over time, this could lead to a significant cumulative loss for landlords.

## Suggested Fix
Use fixed-point arithmetic to maintain precision:
   
```solidity
uint256 constant PRECISION = 1e6;
schnibblesLandlord = (schnibblesTotal * _toiler.latestTaxRate * PRECISION / 1e18) / PRECISION;
```

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L251


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

There are two cases for this issue:

1. Inadequate handling of the exit mechanism in the `_farmPlots` function may result in scenarios where valid plots remain invalid, preventing users from earning rewards. Additionally, the landlord's plot utilization rate may be reduced by 20% or more due to the impact of currency price fluctuations.
2. The second case, while theoretically possible, is less likely to occur but can still affect users. In this situation, the landlord cannot receive rewards if the staked user does not perform any operations, and the landlord cannot do anything to trigger the rewards. Although this situation exists in theory, users will be motivated to collect rewards to end this state. However, the landlord's time will be affected as it depends on the actions of the staked user.

## Proof of Concept

For the second case, the issue is clear.

The main focus here is the first case, the key point [code snippet](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-07-munchables/blob/main/src/managers/LandManager.sol#L251) in the `_farmPlots` function:

```solidity
            if (_toiler.dirty) continue;
```

```solidity
            landlord = _toiler.landlord;
            // use last updated plot metadata time if the plot id doesn't fit
            // track a dirty bool to signify this was done once
            // the edge case where this doesnt work is if the user hasnt farmed in a while and the landlord
            // updates their plots multiple times. then the last updated time will be the last time they updated their plot details
            // instead of the first
            if (_getNumPlots(landlord) < _toiler.plotId) {
                timestamp = plotMetadata[landlord].lastUpdated;
                toilerState[tokenId].dirty = true;
            }
```

Consider the following scenario:

1. A plot becomes invalid due to reduced locked funds or token price drop, and the dirty flag will be set after the user's daily farm (user behavior is uncertain, but what is clear is that users may have a need for daily harvesting that).
2. If funds are relocked or the price rises, the plot remains invalid since the dirty flag isn't reset.
3. Users must restake to earn rewards; otherwise, they receive nothing even if the plot is valid again.

For the landlord, he has to wait for other users to perform operations. Even if he wants to lock more funds to remedy the invalid plot caused by the price drop, it will be of no avail. If the staked user wants to act maliciously or doesn't notice this, it could result in a denial of service for the landlord.

Unlike the effect of calling lock/unlock directly, price changes are beyond the control of users.

As an example, ETH's price fluctuations in the last month have ranged from around [2800-3500 (refer CMC)](https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/ethereum/), the percentage change in the price of ETH over the last 30 days is approximately 20%.
 ​
This means that for a landlord who locks in ETH, 20% of his plots may remain “invalid” due to price fluctuations, while the ETH price will keep changing, which will reduce the landlord's utilization of his plots by 20%.

## Tools Used

Manual

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

1. If the plot is no longer available (unlocking funds/price change), remove the munchable occupying the plot directly during function processing (unlock) or give the landlord the option of triggering an unstake operation (Since no revenue is generated when plots are invalidated after farming and dirty flag are set up, there is no loss for staked munchable users and there is an opportunity to shift the gas cost).

2. Landlords should have the option to set a maximum farming time for plots. This should be a two-way choice. Once farming is complete, both the landlord and the user can opt out (or harvest) and move on to the next round of farming. This mitigation is also an alternative solution to the known critical problem described in the README (the edge case where plots are updated multiple times) by adding a variable that keeps a record of the actual farming time, and the validity time of the plots affected by the lock/unlock operations is stored. (More details will be discussed in that issue)
















## Assessed type

Context

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
In the `LandManager contract`, certain constraints are enforced on accounts, such as ensuring that `landlord != mainAccount` and limiting `munchablesStaked[mainAccount].length` to a maximum of 10. However, it's still possible to create multiple accounts to bypass checks: these checks can be easily bypassed by creating and registering another account or by transferring NFTs to another account to perform staking.


## Proof of Concept
The contract enforces the following constraints, such as ensuring that `landlord != mainAccount` and limiting `munchablesStaked[mainAccount].length` to a maximum of 10.

```solidity
@=>     if (landlord == mainAccount) revert CantStakeToSelfError();
        if (plotOccupied[landlord][plotId].occupied) // @note front-run to take?
            revert OccupiedPlotError(landlord, plotId);
@=>     if (munchablesStaked[mainAccount].length > 10)
            revert TooManyStakedMunchiesError();
        if (munchNFT.ownerOf(tokenId) != mainAccount)
            revert InvalidOwnerError();
```

It's still possible to create multiple accounts to bypass checks:

1. Creating and Registering Another Account: A user can create a new account and register it to avoid the `CantStakeToSelfError`.
2. Transferring NFTs: Users can transfer their NFTs to another account and perform staking from that account, bypassing the `TooManyStakedMunchiesError`.

## Tools Used

Manual

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

To mitigate this issue, try implement account whitelisting mechanism.

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
1.  All tax rates and the price per plot could be set to zero, fundamentally breaking the economic model of the system.
2.  With MIN_TAX_RATE and MAX_TAX_RATE potentially set to zero, the updateTaxRate() function's checks become meaningless allowing any tax rate to be set.
3.  If PRICE_PER_PLOT is zero, users might be able to acquire land for free leading to economic imbalance and potential system abuse.
4.  Zero-value BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE could disrupt any reward or incentive mechanisms based on this rate.

## Proof of Concept
In the `LandManager` contract's `_reconfigure()` function, critical parameters such as `MIN_TAX_RATE`, `MAX_TAX_RATE`, `DEFAULT_TAX_RATE`, `BASE_SCHNIBBLE_RATE`, and `PRICE_PER_PLOT ` are being initialized using incorrect storage keys. Instead of using keys specific to these parameters, the function is using keys that appear to be related to other contract addresses or unrelated configurations


These keys `(LockManager, AccountManager, ClaimManager, MigrationManager)` are likely meant for retrieving contract addresses not numerical values for tax rates and prices. Moreover, the getUint() function does not revert on non-existent keys but returns zero. This means that if these incorrect keys don't exist in the configuration (which is likely), all these critical parameters will be silently initialized to zero.

## Tools Used
Manual review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
1. Use the correct keys for each parameter ensuring they match the keys used when setting these values in the configuration contract.
2. Implement checks in the `_reconfigure` function to ensure that retrieved values are non-zero and within expected ranges: i.e
```
MIN_TAX_RATE = configStorage.getUint(StorageKey.MinTaxRate);
require(MIN_TAX_RATE > 0, "MIN_TAX_RATE not set");

MAX_TAX_RATE = configStorage.getUint(StorageKey.MaxTaxRate);
require(MAX_TAX_RATE > MIN_TAX_RATE, "Invalid MAX_TAX_RATE");

//similar for the other two values.

```


## Assessed type

# Lines of code

# Vulnerability details

## Impact

As AccountManager.addSubAccount() can arbitrarily overwrite anyone’s main account, an attacker can prevent a chosen victim from updating their tax rate, which results in unfair game restrictions for the victim.


## Proof of Concept

Consider the following scenario:

1. Assume Alice is a registered landlord.
2. Bob calls `AccountManager.addSubAccount(alice)` which sets `mainAccounts[alice]` to Bob’s address.
3. Alice wants to update her tax rate, so she calls `LandManager.updateTaxRate()`. However, this call will update the tax rate of Bob’s plot instead because `landlord` (the return value of `_getMainAccountRequireRegistered(msg.sender)`) is Bob’s address at this point. Hence, Alice will never be able to update her tax rate

## Tools Used

Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

The AccountManager logic must be reworked to ensure that no authorized party can arbitrarily modify someone’s main account address. The simplest fix would be to remove the entire concept of subaccount. If that’s not feasible, one potential mitigation is to require an approval signature from the original main account’s address in order to override the original main account address.

It is also important to ensure that `updateTaxRate()` offers the original landlord a way to update their tax rate, even if the main account changed. 


## Assessed type

Access Control

At the end of the `_farmPlots()` function, the contract makes an external call to the updatePlayer() function in the accountManager contract:

However, the updatePlayer() has an onlyConfiguredContract3() modifier which LandManager hasn't been added to yet, this will cause the call to updatePlayer() to revert causing most operations to fail.

Either remove the call to the updatePlayer or add the LandManager to the onlyConfiguredContract3() modifier in the accountManager.

# Vulnerability details

## Impact

The `stakeMunchable` function, allows user to stake their munchables and earn rewards. The line below, transfers the munchNFT to the contract
```solidity
        munchNFT.transferFrom(mainAccount, address(this), tokenId); //transferFrom(address from, address to, uint256 tokenId)
```
As we know `transferFrom` returns a `boolean` according to [OZ docs](https://docs.openzeppelin.com/contracts/4.x/api/token/erc20#IERC20-transferFrom-address-address-uint256-).
Hence, in case of failure the function won't be notified, or it won't revert. It will continue the staking process. 

The following part stakes and updates metadata of munchables.
```solidity
        plotOccupied[landlord][plotId] = Plot({
            occupied: true,
            tokenId: tokenId
        });

        munchablesStaked[mainAccount].push(tokenId);
        munchableOwner[tokenId] = mainAccount;

        toilerState[tokenId] = ToilerState({
            lastToilDate: block.timestamp,
            plotId: plotId,
            landlord: landlord,
            latestTaxRate: plotMetadata[landlord].currentTaxRate,
            dirty: false
        })
```
Hence, in case of `transferFrom` failure this part would continue successfully. Which should not happen in case of transaction failure.

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
If value of `lockedTokens[_player][configuredTokenContracts[i]].quantity *configuredTokens[configuredTokenContracts[i]].usdPrice` is less than or equal to `1e10` , `_getNumPlots will return wrong value

The `_getNumPlots` function in `LandManager.sol` returns -
```
lockManager.getLockedWeightedValue(_account) / PRICE_PER_PLOT
```
Which is calling the `getLockedWeightedValue` function from `LockManager.sol` contract. 
The calculation of `lockedWeighted` is as follows
```
 lockedWeighted +=(deltaDecimal * lockedTokens[_player][configuredTokenContracts[i]].quantity *configuredTokens[configuredTokenContracts[i]].usdPrice) /1e18;
```
The calculation of `deltaDecimal ` is as follows - 
```
uint256 deltaDecimal = 10 **(18 - configuredTokens[configuredTokenContracts[i]].decimals);
```
The `configuredTokens` here is `MunchTokens` which contains `1e12` decimals, hence `deltaDecimal` = 10e(18-12)=10e6 

So for correct calculation of `lockedWeighted ` , `lockedTokens[_player][configuredTokenContracts[i]].quantity *configuredTokens[configuredTokenContracts[i]].usdPrice` must be in the range of `1e11` 

If it has decimals less than 11 then it would cause the value to return 0.
As in solidity -> 10e6*1e10=1e17/1e18 , would return 0.

If the value returned is wrong then the `_getNumPlots` will also return wrong value which would then effect the functionality of the other functions which is using `_getNumPlots` like `_farmPlots` , `transferToUnoccupiedPlot` , `stakeMunchable` function.



## Proof of Concept
